data.title: SEC Sues Eight Colorado Entities Over Alleged $37 Million Crypto Platform Fraud
data.description:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has sued eight Colorado-based entities—Advisor WeChat Capital, Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance Ltd., HB Wealth Advisors, IdeaCrypto Exchange LLC, Convergent Wealth Advisors Inc., RealSimple Crypto Exchange Inc., Associated Wealth Advisors Ltd. and Essential Crypto Exchange—alleging they used fake cryptocurrency trading platforms to defraud U.S. investors of more than $37 million. According to Foresight News, the SEC said the scheme’s operators may be based overseas.

The defendants allegedly attracted investors through social media ads and group or private chats, initially offering advice on U.S. stock trading before steering people to deposit funds on fake crypto platforms. They allegedly fabricated SEC certificates and used filings submitted to the SEC, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) or the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to make the businesses appear legitimate.

The alleged scheme operated from August 2024 to May 2026 and involved four groups of fake investment advisers and trading platforms. Each group operated for several months before being replaced. The SEC filed its lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado and is seeking permanent injunctions, recovery of alleged illicit proceeds and civil penalties.

data.title: STOCKS | NetEase Gaming Revenue Falls 1.7%, Shares Drop 11.39%; Ding Lei Says Short Dramas Will Affect Games
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, NetEase founder and CEO Ding Lei said short-form dramas have grown explosively this year and strongly attract users’ attention, which will affect games in the short term. He made the remarks on the evening of November 19 during NetEase’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call, in response to a question about the impact of short-form dramas on the gaming industry.

NetEase reported third-quarter net revenue of 27.9 billion yuan, down 1.8% year over year, and net profit attributable to company shareholders of 8.4 billion yuan, down about 2.5%. Revenue from games and related value-added services, its largest revenue source, fell 1.7% year over year to 22.9 billion yuan. It was the first year-over-year decline for the business since the third quarter of 2024; revenue grew 6.9% and 9.7% year over year in the first and second quarters, respectively. NetEase’s gross margin fell 2% quarter over quarter to 69%, as its high-profit gaming business underperformed.

NetEase shares fell 11.39% by the U.S. market close on November 20 (UTC+8).

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | CICC Wealth Futures: Liquidity Is a Clearer Pressure on Precious Metals Than High Rates
data.description: According to Jin10, CICC Wealth Futures said gold continued to fall, briefly dropping below $3,600 per ounce, while international silver fell from a year-to-date high of $121 per ounce to $42. It cited a strong U.S. dollar, high oil prices and persistently elevated inflation as ongoing pressures on precious metals. Beyond the valuation pressure from high interest rates, liquidity was a more evident factor, particularly gold selling triggered by sell-offs in U.S. equities, which it said had often occurred historically. The firm advised waiting patiently for gold's decline to end.

data.title: Citi Cuts Alibaba ADR and Hong Kong Share Targets After Cloud Growth Outlook Slows
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Alibaba said in its quarterly report on Thursday that cloud services revenue growth is expected to slow next year from the current 53% to 30%-45%, before returning to above 50% in calendar 2028. Citi cut its price targets for Alibaba ADRs and Hong Kong shares to $160 and HK$159, respectively, citing downward revisions to industry-wide valuations.

Citi analysts including Alicia Yap said Alibaba’s lower cloud revenue growth guidance was a pragmatic response to evolving restrictions on computing-power exports, while its long-term AI ambitions remained unchanged. They said the company’s reaffirmation of its 2030 and 2031 cloud business targets showed that short-term policy headwinds had not changed long-term demand opportunities.

Citi said policy changes had increased uncertainty around capacity expansion, but Alibaba’s full-stack AI technology based on its self-developed chips would put it in a relatively more favorable position.

data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Three Major Indices Fall Over 2% as Dow Drops Below 50,000; Anthropic Debuts With 17% Gain
data.description: U.S. stocks tumbled on Friday, with major indices hitting intraday lows just as AI newcomer Anthropic began trading. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to close at 49,097.06, its first close below 50,000 since June. The S&P 500 dropped 147.80 points, or 2.02%, to 7,175.83, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 550.69 points, or 2.25%, to 23,879.20. Anthropic listed on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, opening near midday at $111.50, a 34% jump from its IPO price of $83 per share, which was set above the expected range. The stock pulled back about 13% from its opening highs, ending the day with a 17% gain. Following Anthropic's debut, investors appeared to lock in profits from the AI rally, sending the VIX fear gauge as high as nearly 29, a March intraday high, with the latest reading still above 28. Chip stocks including NVIDIA and Micron Technology gave back gains, while Microsoft and Meta also weakened. AMD fell more than 7% after hedge fund Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position. Aleks Spencer, chief investment officer at Bogart Wealth, said the IPO was a key test for the tech sector, noting that Anthropic could become a new benchmark for AI sentiment following NVIDIA's recent turmoil, with the market facing significant uncertainty and volatility. Spencer added that elevated market sentiment presents an opportunity to take profits. According to Sina Finance, investors have grown cautious on AI, scrutinizing whether massive computing investments can translate into real profits. The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) fell nearly 14% this month; NVIDIA dropped 28% as it grappled with the impact of CEO Jensen Huang's resignation; CoreWeave shares fell 18% in November, with its bond yields briefly exceeding 16%. Baird technology strategist Ted Mortonson called the day's moves inconclusive, comparing Anthropic's debut to casino trading, saying what matters is the company's trajectory over the next three years.

data.title: Sky Founder Says Protocol Is Operating Normally as Committee Launches 5.25 Million USDS Buyback
data.description:
Sky Protocol founder Rune Christensen said the protocol is operating normally and financially sound, while Sky’s core committee announced a one-time 5.25 million USDS buyback. According to Odaily, Christensen said recent reports about Sky were overstated, USDS remains overcollateralized with about $10 billion in asset backing, and the protocol’s mechanisms are working as designed.

Sky processed more than $2 billion in outflows over the past 24 hours, Christensen said. Liquidity supporting the stablecoin’s peg remained above $2 billion and has since risen to more than $2.25 billion. Sky generated about $400 million in revenue over the past year.

The buyback will follow the process set out in Sky Atlas, with 750,000 USDS allocated each day for seven consecutive days, for a total of 5.25 million USDS.

data.title: Tom Lee Says Selling the S&P 500 Amid Rising Pessimism Could Mean Selling at the Bottom
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee said worsening market pessimism may make selling now tantamount to selling at the bottom. He said the market decline reflects investors reducing risk exposure amid multiple concerns rather than deteriorating fundamentals.

Over the past 15 years, the S&P 500 rose in the week after six consecutive trading-day declines in all 10 observed cases, gaining an average of 2.7% and a median of 2.1%. Lee also put the probability of the index rising Friday at 70%.
